chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Muhammad ibn Ajlan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Place him with a gentle placing. So when you place him in his grave (lahd), let the closest of the people to his head mention the Name of Allah upon him, and send blessings upon the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), and seek refuge from Satan, and let him recite the Opening of the Book (Al-Fatiha), and the Two Protecting Chapters (Al-Mu'awwidhatayn), and 'Say: He is Allah, One' (Al-Ikhlas), and the Verse of the Throne (Ayat al-Kursi). And if he is able to bare his cheek and press it against the ground, he should do so, and he should testify and mention whatever he knows until he reaches his companion.

key_terms.آيَةَ الْكُرْسِيِّ: The Verse of the Throne, referring to Ayat al-Kursi (Quran 2:255)
key_terms.الْمُعَوِّذَتَيْنِ: The Two Protecting Chapters, referring to Surah Al-Falaq and Surah An-Nas
key_terms.فَاتِحَةَ الْكِتَابِ: The Opening of the Book, referring to Surah Al-Fatiha
key_terms.قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ: Say: He is Allah, One, referring to Surah Al-Ikhlas
key_terms.لَحْدِهِ: The grave, specifically the niche dug into the side of the grave
key_terms.يَحْسِرَ: To bare or uncover (specifically the cheek)
key_terms.يُلْزِقَهُ بِالْأَرْضِ: To press it against the ground

ai.seo_question: What are the recommended recitations and actions when placing the deceased in the grave according to Shia tradition?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the specific etiquette for burial, emphasizing the spiritual protection of the deceased through the recitation of key Quranic chapters and supplications by those closest to the head. It highlights the Shia practice of ensuring the deceased is gently placed and accompanied by prayers for deliverance from Satan's whispers, reflecting the belief in the soul's journey in the grave.

en.hubeali:
Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Muhammad Bin Ajlan, 
from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Place him with a gentle placing. So when you place him in his chasm (Lahad), so let the the closest of the people from what follows his head mention the Name of Allahazwj upon him, and he should send Blessings upon the Prophetsaww, and seek Refuge from the Satanla, and let him recite the Opening of the Book (Chapter 1), and the Maw’azatayn (Chapters 113 & 114), and Ayat Al Kursy (Chapter 2:255). And if he is able to bare his cheek (of the deceased) and paste his cheek with the ground, so he should do so, and he should testify and mention whatever he knows until he ends up to his companion’.
en.sarwar: 4. Sahl ibn Ziyad has narrated from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Muhammad ibn ‘Ajlan who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, Alayhi al-Salam, has

said to place a deceased gently in the grave. The person from the side of his head, when he is placed in the grave, should speak of the names of Allah. He should also say ‘Allahumma Salli ‘Ala Muhammad wa ‘Ali Muhammad (O Allah grant Muhammad and his family a compensation worthy of their serving Your cause).’ He should ask protection with Allah against Satan; read al-Fatihah al-Kitab, chapters 113, 114, 112 of the Holy Quran and Ayatu al-Kursiy. If possible, one should place the side of his face on the soil without covering, say the testimonies, and speak of Allah whatever he knows until he is in the presence of his guardian (Imam al-Mahdi).”
